purpose: Read-mode editorial storyboard; original diagrams specified, not rendered assets.

modeContract.switchBehavior: Preserve shared lesson, practice answers, progress and preferences. Switching mode never resets or completes a lesson. Map Watch chapter cues to Read panel IDs; when no precise cue exists, switch at the same lesson and announce that position.
modeContract.fullText: Always expose Full lesson text as semantic HTML, including every original content paragraph, activity, knowledge check and referenced source. Never hide the only accessible equivalent behind animation.
modeContract.practice: Use the identical source activity and knowledgeCheck in both modes. Do not duplicate scoring or alter answer IDs.
modeContract.watchUnavailable: Keep Read accessible. Label Watch unavailable or preparing honestly; never display a fake playable asset.

deliveryNote: Compact derivative. Read original course JSON for verbatim content, activities, checks, source links and assessment keys. All diagrams are specified-not-rendered native HTML/CSS or accessible SVG. No production artwork is claimed. Canonical design artifact is read-storyboards.json.

panelDefaults.interaction: Explicit Next/Back and optional native details; no auto-advance. Keep callouts visible; full source text remains available.
panelDefaults.visualAssetType: original semantic diagram or native case card
panelDefaults.textEquivalent: Use panel copy plus mapped source paragraphs; use original numerical tables where specified.

lessons.title: A new tool is not yet a new habit

panels.title: Specify the behavior
copy: Before shift end, every open ticket needs an owner and a next action.
panels.visualSpecification: Original queue-card illustration with two labeled fields; incomplete and complete handoffs compared.

panels.title: Five change questions
copy: Awareness: why?
Desire: choose to engage?
Knowledge: what to do?
Ability: do it?
Reinforcement: sustain it?
panels.visualSpecification: Five equal-weight labeled cards in reading order, not a scored diagnostic or maturity ranking.
panels.callout: ADKAR concerns individual change within a wider approach; this is an independent sample.

panels.title: Look for observed performance
copy: Explaining the steps suggests Knowledge.
A realistic completed handoff provides Ability evidence.
panels.visualSpecification: Explain / Perform cards each with its own evidence slot.
panels.callout: Treat barriers as hypotheses to discuss, not labels for people.

panels.title: Try the decision, then check your reasoning
copy: Choose a response and explain the evidence behind it.
Read the option-specific feedback, then try the knowledge check.
panels.visualSpecification: One original case card above a semantic radio-choice group. Feedback appears directly under the chosen option; knowledge check follows as a separate step in the same panel. No decorative character art needed.
panels.callout: Practice remains available in both Read and Watch. Selected-response success does not establish production mastery.

panels.title: Alex asks why
copy: Ask about missed handoffs.
Use an accurate, anonymized example.
Ask Alex to explain the reason back.
panels.visualSpecification: Original dialogue cards labeled Alex and Coach; show the next question before the suggested response.

panels.title: Priya raises a concern
copy: Acknowledge the concern about ranking.
Verify data-use rules before reassuring.
Invite specific questions.
panels.visualSpecification: A concern card linked to a Verify policy card; no stock-photo emotional stereotypes.
panels.callout: Do not promise tracking will never affect performance management unless approved and true.

panels.title: Understanding is not willingness
copy: Concerns may expose a real design problem.
Practice a neutral question and one fact to verify.
panels.visualSpecification: Awareness and Desire evidence columns with a short private rehearsal prompt.
panels.callout: Do not assume reluctance means laziness.

panels.title: Mateo needs a decision rule
copy: Demonstrate Assign versus Transfer.
Ask which action fits a new ticket and why.
panels.visualSpecification: Two synthetic action cards with a sample unowned ticket; reveal model reasoning.

panels.title: Nia needs workable conditions
copy: She knows the steps.
Her account cannot assign tickets; she lacks practice cover.
Resolve access properly and provide protected practice.
panels.visualSpecification: Knowledge evidence card beside two practical blockers: access and time.
panels.callout: Another slide deck does not grant permissions.

panels.title: Demonstrate, practice, observe
copy: Show one owner-and-next-action example.
Let the learner try a new ticket without hints.
Investigate obstacles before prescribing instruction.
panels.visualSpecification: Three-step practice sequence; accommodation/access checklist remains visible.
panels.callout: A system obstacle is not a character flaw.

panels.title: The shortcut returns
copy: A supervisor starts accepting email handoffs again.
People follow that example despite remembering the queue steps.
panels.visualSpecification: Two labeled handoff routes with a supervisor cue, without implying the tool automatically enforces behavior.

panels.title: Reinforce the intended behavior
copy: Ask why the shortcut returned.
Remove real friction.
Agree the standard and recognize accurate work.
panels.visualSpecification: A feedback loop from observation to conversation to support to review.
panels.callout: Completion counts do not establish handoff quality; raw ticket rewards can distort behavior.

panels.title: Review without ranking people
copy: Check five agreed sample handoffs on Friday.
Inspect owner and next action; ask about obstacles.
Review the next step Tuesday.
panels.visualSpecification: Compact review-plan card with behavior, sample, conversation and review date fields.
panels.callout: Practice dates and sample size are not validated thresholds. Minimize personal data.
